metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.00), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and apply gradual decay toward mean.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; cap forecast range within ±10% of recent 7-day moving average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast exceeds 20% above recent 14-day high, reduce by 15–25% unless event-driven.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after spike, model often fails to recognize it; add 3–5 day lag correction for downward momentum.
- In absence of sentiment signals, assume neutral market; avoid aggressive directional forecasts; use 14-day SMA as baseline anchor.
